paper.title: Adapting to Delays and Data in Adversarial Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial multi-armed bandit with delayed feedback (oblivious losses and delays)
unmapped: Delays are arbitrary (non-uniform), chosen obliviously in advance, possibly jointly with losses; delays become known only when the feedback arrives
settings.definition_quote: In the delayed-feedback setting we consider, ... after taking an action $A_t$ in time step $t$, the learner observes the loss $\ell_{t, A_t}$ only after a delay of $d_t$ time steps ... We assume that the sequence of delays $(d_t)_t$ is selected before the process starts, obliviously to the actions of the learner.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial multi-armed bandit with delayed feedback, delay known at decision time (DeDa-Exp3)
unmapped: The learner knows the delay d_t of each round at decision time, or an a priori upper bound on the maximum delay
Delays are arbitrary (non-uniform), chosen obliviously in advance
settings.definition_quote: The algorithm keeps track of the largest delay ($d^\star_t$) and, similarly to \citet{thune19}, to do so it needs to observe the delay for action $A_t$ in advance. This can be avoided if the algorithm has access to an a priori upper bound $d^B$ on the maximum delay

algorithms.name: DAda-Exp3 with implicit exploration loss estimates
DeDa-Exp3 (Delay and Data Adaptive Exp3)
requires_knowledge_of: delay of each round at decision time (or upper bound on max delay)

tuning: eta_t = sqrt(log(K)/(tK + sum_{s<=t} tau_s)), tau_s = number of missing feedbacks at time s

source.label: cor:simple
source.quote: With $\eta_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(K)}{tK + \sum_{s=1}^t \tau_s}}$, the regret of the \adaexp algorithm can be bounded as $R_T \le 3\sqrt{\log(K)\left(TK + D \right)}$.

results.notes: Paper's D is the cumulative delay, not a fixed delay, hence D_cum. Regret is sum E[loss] minus loss of fixed arm under oblivious adversary. Step size uses only observed info, so anytime and no knowledge of delays.

bound.expression_latex: 2\sqrt{3\log(K)\left( 2 K T + D \right)} + \left(2\sqrt{\frac{2 TK + D}{3\log(K)}} + d^\star +2\right)\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2}

source.label: cor:simple-high-prob
source.quote: With $\eta_t=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{3 \log(K)}{2 tK + \sum_{s=1}^t \tau_s}}$, under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-high-prob}, $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \left(\ell_{t,A_t} - \ell_{t, A^\star}\right) \le 2\sqrt{3\log(K)\left( 2 K T + D \right)} + \left(2\sqrt{\frac{2 TK + D}{3\log(K)}} + d^\star +2\right)\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2}$.

results.notes: Holds w.p. at least 1-delta against an arbitrary fixed arm A*. Derived from Theorem 4.1 (general step-size bound, not recorded separately).

symbols.Phi_skip: min over subsets R of [T] of (|R| + sqrt(D_Rbar*log(K))), where D_Rbar is the cumulative delay of rounds not in R

tuning: eta_t = sqrt(log(K)/(tK + sum_{s<=t} tilde_tau_s)) with skipping-based counted missing feedbacks

source.quote: (i) Bound in expectation: The expected regret of the \adaexp algorithm with loss estimates \eqref{eq:ellhat1} and step sizes $\eta_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(K)}{tK + \sum_{s=1}^t \dtau_t}}$ can be bounded as $\sum_{t=1}^{T} (\EE{\ell_{t,A_t}} - \ell_{t, A^\star}) \le 3\sqrt{TK\log(K)} + 10 \max\{2 \log K, \min_{R \subset [T]} (|R| + \sqrt{D_{\bar{R}}\log(K)})\}$

results.notes: Skipping procedure adopted from Zimmert & Seldin (2019).

symbols.Phi_skip: min over subsets R of [T] of (|R| + sqrt(D_Rbar*log(K))), where D_Rbar is the cumulative delay of rounds not in R

tuning: implicit exploration estimates with eta_t = gamma_t = (1/2) sqrt(3 log(K)/(2tK + sum_{s<=t} tau_s)) (with skipping)

source.quote: (ii) High-probability bound: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. The regret of the \adaexp algorithm with loss estimates \eqref{eq:ellhat-IX} and step sizes $\eta_t=\gamma_t=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{3 \log(K)}{2 tK + \sum_{s=1}^t \tau_s}}$ can be bounded, with probability at least $1-\delta$, as ... where $c_1=2\sqrt{6}$, $c_2=\sqrt{2/3}$, $c_3=4(\sqrt{3}+1)$, and $c_4=1+2/\sqrt{3}$.

results.notes: Removes the d* dependence of Corollary 4.2 via skipping.

symbols.Lambda_DD: sum_t ( sum_{s in O_t union D_t} E[l_{s,A_s} l_{t,A_s}] + sum_i l_{t,i} ), data- and delay-dependent quantity

tuning: step size eta_t^{-1} = (4 d*_t^2 + 6 d*_t + 2)/log K + sqrt(L^bck_t / log K), gamma_t = eta_t

source.label: thm:deda-exp3
source.quote: If the step-sizes are given by \eqref{eq:adaptive-step-mixed-delay-and-data}, then \dedaexp satisfies $\sum_{t=1}^{T} (\EE{\ell_{t,A_t}} - \ell_{t, A^\star}) \le C_T + c\sqrt{\log(K)\sum_{t = 1}^{T}(\sum_{s \in O_t \cup D_t} \EE{\ell_{s,A_s}\ell_{t,A_s}} + \sum_{i=1}^K \ell_{t,i})}$, where $C_T = 4 (d^\star_T)^2 + 6 d^\star_T + 2$, $c = 2+\sqrt{2}$

results.notes: Data-dependent quantity declared as Lambda_DD. Algorithm requires delay at decision time or an upper bound on max delay.

source.quote: Bounding the losses by $1$, this gives a regret upper bound \[ R_T \le C_T + c \sqrt{\log(K) \left(KT + 2\sum_{t=1}^T d_t\right)}~. \]

results.notes: Stated in a remark as a consequence of Theorem 6.2.

symbols.L_sum: sum over arms of cumulative losses, sum_i L_{T,i}

source.quote: Hence, \emph{the effect of the delay on the regret scales only with the loss of the optimal arm}: \[ R_T \le 2 C'_T + 4c'\sqrt{d^\star_T L_{T,A^*}/2} + 2 c'\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^K L_{T,i}}. \]

results.notes: C'_T = C_T + c'^2 d*_T with c' = c sqrt(log K), C_T = 4d*^2+6d*+2, c = 2+sqrt(2); expanded in the expression. Derived in a remark.
